resumen: Standing with the kettlebell held overhead on a straight arm, you lean the torso to the opposite side, bringing the other hand to the foot, eyes on the kettlebell. It works the obliques, the hips and shoulder stability.
ejecucion: Clean the kettlebell or bring it to your shoulder with both hands, then press it overhead with a straight arm; set your feet slightly wider than your hips, toes turned about 45° away from the kettlebell side.
Look at the kettlebell and push your hips towards the kettlebell side as your torso leans to the other side.

Slide your free hand down the inside of the free-side leg, without rounding your back, as far as you can, ideally to your foot; the leg on the kettlebell side stays straight and the top arm always vertical.
Come back up with your hips until you are standing; when you finish, switch sides.
Start without weight or with a very light one: if the top arm tilts or the shoulder hurts, do not load it.
When you finish, lower the kettlebell to your shoulder, then to the floor with both hands.
matices: We have found no study measuring the kettlebell windmill. The shoulder has to hold the load overhead while the torso leans and the hips move, so it demands mobility and stability; that is why we place it after the press and the Turkish get-up.
